I’m using the `crimes-codebase-risk` review workflow because this is a contract audit driven by `crimes scan`. I’ll verify each finding against the client and API source, then separate production-breaking disagreements from naming-only risk.

The repository-local skill path advertised for this checkout isn’t present at that location, so I’m locating the installed copy before continuing. The review itself is unaffected; I haven’t made any changes.

The skill file is genuinely absent from this evaluation checkout, so I’m proceeding with the repository’s documented fallback: a read-only JSON scan plus direct source inspection. I’m checking all endpoints and types, not treating every scanner finding as a wire-contract defect.

Direct inspection exposes more wire-level drift than the five scan findings alone: both “workspace” routes miss the API, both parameterized URLs send the literal `:id`, and the plan-change call omits the backend’s required `plan` parameter. I’m now checking framework semantics and distinguishing latent type drift from immediate 404/405/422 failures.

The client and API disagree on every operation except the overlapping response fields. Three calls hard-fail; the seats call is worse because it can return plausible but incorrect data.

| Rank | Disagreement | Production failure |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `changeWorkspacePlan` sends `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan`; the API declares `POST /api/teams/{team_id}/plan`. The client also ignores both `id` and `plan`. ([client:33](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:33>), [API:25](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:25>)) | Currently always **405**. Changing only the method then produces **422**, because FastAPI treats `plan: str` as a required query parameter and the client sends none. Fixing that too still sends the literal team ID `:id`. |
| 2 | `workspaceSeats(id)` sends the literal `/api/teams/:id/seats`. The API accepts that as `team_id=":id"` and then ignores the identifier, always calculating seats for `Plan.FREE`. ([client:27](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:27>), [API:20](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:20>)) | **200 with incorrect data:** every workspace appears to have one seat. This silent billing/entitlement error is harder to detect than a 4xx. |
| 3 | `createWorkspace` calls `POST /api/workspaces`; the API exposes `POST /api/teams`. It also sends no body, while `payload: dict` is required. ([client:22](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:22>), [API:15](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:15>)) | Currently **404**. Correcting only the path exposes a second failure: **422** for the missing request body. |
| 4 | `getWorkspace` calls `/api/workspaces/{id}`; the API exposes `/api/teams/{team_id}`. ([client:17](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:17>), [API:10](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10>)) | Always **404**. The scan missed this assembled URL. |
| 5 | Plan sets differ: TypeScript has `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`; Python has `free`, `pro`, `team`, `scale`. ([client:10](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10>), [plans:10](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/31ec6848-6241-4e9f-8dd7-0c4cc25d2561/scratchpad/eval-022/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10>)) | Latent incompatibility: `team` or `scale` responses enter the client without runtime validation and can break labels, pricing, or exhaustive branches. Conversely, the client can submit `enterprise`, which is not a canonical backend plan. |
| 6 | Despite defining `Plan`, the update API accepts `plan: str`. | Once the transport errors are fixed, `enterprise` or any arbitrary string receives a successful response instead of validation. In a real persistence implementation this could create invalid billing state. |
| 7 | The same tenant concept is called “workspace” in TypeScript and “team” in Python. | No runtime failure by itself, but it already contributed to the divergent paths and makes cross-boundary changes easier to miss. |

A further failure amplifier is that none of the client calls checks `res.ok`. A 404/405/422 JSON error can therefore be returned to callers as though it were a `Workspace`; `workspaceSeats` instead returns `undefined`.

Of the five scan findings:

- `crime_00001`, `crime_00003`, and `crime_00005` identify real contract drift.
- `crime_00004` is maintenance risk, not an additional runtime mismatch.
- `crime_00002` is not a contract defect: an HTTP GET is appropriate behavior for `getWorkspace`. I would mark it false-positive with:

```bash
crimes feedback 'name_behavior_mismatch::packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts::getWorkspace' \
  --verdict fp \
  --note "getWorkspace performs an HTTP GET; network I/O is expected for a read operation and does not mutate server state."
```

The local runner lacked a `crimes` executable, so I validated the supplied `crimes scan --format json` result directly against all three scanned source files. No files were changed.
